comparison: Both evaluations support the model construction and parameterization claims (C2, C11, C13-C16, C21). OpenEval provides detailed technical validation of SRRW foundation and excluded volume modifications. Peer reviewers affirm the methodology as 'convincing' and recognize the framework's ability to recapitulate experimental properties. Strong agreement on model development.

Both support structural features and biphasic topology claims (C3, C4, C22, C57, C58). OpenEval notes qualitative agreement with ChromSTEM imaging. Peer reviewers affirm the model captures 'local density and large-scale contact structural properties' and find methodology convincing. Strong alignment on structural predictions.

Both support RAD21 depletion predictions and experimental validation (C47-C50, C5). OpenEval provides quantitative details (~20% domain loss prediction vs 80% retention observed). Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly states 'They perform some experiments to compare with model predictions and show consistency between the two.' Strong agreement on experimental validation.

Both support the interpretation of multiple mechanisms contributing to stochastic returns (C52, C53). OpenEval notes this as a reasonable inference from RAD21 depletion data. Peer reviewers implicitly support this conceptual framework, with the first reviewer acknowledging it as 'an interesting alternative to standard molecular dynamics simulations.' Agreement on mechanistic interpretation.

Both support testable predictions about methodological sensitivities (C54, C56, C28). OpenEval details Hi-C insensitivity to volume fraction and density-method predictions. Peer reviewers accept these predictions as part of the model's framework for addressing 'large-scale contact structural properties' alongside local density. Agreement on model predictions.

Divergent evaluations on model scope and capabilities (C60-C63, C67). OpenEval supports claims about spatial scale, nucleosome resolution, and chromosome-scale reach. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, with Reviewer 1 noting significant limitations: model 'cannot fully account for specific mechanisms' like TADs, A/B compartments, and promoter-enhancer loops, and 'excluded volume only impacts locally.' Disagreement on scope claims.

Both support CVC properties and parameter relationships (C28, C33-C35, C37, C45). OpenEval provides detailed validation from Figures 5B, 6, and 9. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings as part of the model's ability to capture density properties and describe chromatin organization at multiple scales. Agreement on parameter dependencies.

Both support local density and domain organization relationships (C37, C41, C45). OpenEval emphasizes Figure 9 evidence for volume fraction-packing parameter correlation and heterogeneity matching PWS data. Peer reviewers accept these as part of the model's density property capabilities. Agreement on density-structure relationships.

Both support stochastic heterogeneity claims (C41, C60). OpenEval notes distribution of Di values demonstrates intrinsic heterogeneity. Reviewer 1 explicitly recognizes this as a strength, stating the model 'may offer an alternative framework to investigate single-cell and population structural properties.' Strong agreement on stochastic capabilities.

Both support nucleosome parameterization and linker length predictions (C17, C18). OpenEval notes predicted linker DNA lengths match literature values. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this as part of model validation, with the first reviewer noting the framework is 'reliable in describing chromatin organization at multiple scales.' Agreement on nucleosome-scale accuracy.

Partial divergence on experimental validation (C35, C20). OpenEval supports quantitative agreement with Ou et al. 2017 data and ChromSTEM imaging. Peer reviewers acknowledge qualitative agreement but Reviewer 1 specifically notes weakness: 'Comparisons with experiments are solid but are not clearly quantified.' Agreement on qualitative validation, concern about quantitative rigor.

Both support bi-continuous organization and functional implications (C23). OpenEval notes consistency with model's stochastic return rules. Peer reviewers implicitly accept functional interpretations, with the first reviewer stating work is 'valuable for the community' and provides 'solid evidence.' Agreement on structural-functional relationships.

Both support nucleosome resolution claims (C61). OpenEval emphasizes nucleosome resolution with accurate linker lengths as demonstrated throughout results. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this as part of the model's multi-scale reliability without specific challenge. Agreement on resolution capabilities.

OpenEval evaluates C55 (cancer biology background claim about nuclear abnormalities) as supported by historical citation to Hansemann, 1890. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this background/motivational claim.
OpenEval evaluates C6 (established chromatin structure knowledge) as supported background information. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this contextual claim.

OpenEval evaluates experimental methods (C68-C70) as adequately described methodological details with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these methodological claims.
